newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares closed up, despite a slide in the gold index, as positive sentiment continued to support the market, dealers said on Friday.
President Nelson Mandela's speech at the opening of parliament in Cape Town contained no surprises and was seen underpinning a recent upsurge in confidence -- without triggering off a major rally.
"It was a good speech. The market sees it in a positive light but it contained no big news," one dealer said.

The all-share index ended up 16.0 points to 6,879.6 as the industrial index put on 22.6 points to 8,203.0. But the gold index took a hammering as the bullion price dropped to its lowest levels for nearly four years.
The index shed 30.0 points, or 2.16 percent, to 1,357.5. Among losers in the sector were Amgold which shed 975 cents to 308.00 rand and Goldfields which lost 400 cents to 113.00 rand.
Some analysts have speculated that the gold price may try and test levels in the low $330s an ounce range, spelling more gloom for South African gold shares.
Compounding the woes the rand gold price fell to its lowest level in eleven months on Friday on the dollar gold price and as the rand continued its rally against the U.S. unit.
Analysts said the falling price held dire prospects for South African gold mines in the first quarter of this year.
"I think in general a lot of operations are going to be very marginalised in the current quarter," said Dean Cunningham, gold analyst at stockbrokers Fergusson Bros.
However, the surging rand, strong bond market and good outlook for interest rates are still underpinning the positive mood in the rest of the market.
South African blue chips are still attracting good overseas and foreign institutional interest and got a late boost from market pleasing U.S. jobless figures.
Among gainers were Barlow at 100 cents up to 51.00 rand and Gencor up 45 cents to 19.00 rand. Losers were Richemont which was off 50 cents to 61.00 rand and Ingwe Coal at 30.75 rand, down 25 cents.
Volumes were high at 850 million rands worth of trade, but off Thursday's record-breaking levels of more than one billion rands.
Dealers said the rise would continue next week. "It will continue where it left off," one dealer said.
The futures market also reacted positvely to the day's news, without making any heady gains.
The all-share March contract was at 6,380/90 from 6,350 as the industrials contract was at 8,003/08 from 7,958. Inevitably the ailing gold contrcat took a further knock and was at 935/50 from 959.
